messages:
emily_cs: Heads up — Acme (acct 54321) flagged a month-end reconciliation mismatch. Invoice INV-2026-03-31-54321 = $12,345.67 but the dashboard total is $11,987.40. Customer wants line-item breakdown and explanation. I attached screenshots to the ticket.
raj_support: Thanks, Emily. Do we have the invoice JSON and the exact dashboard query they ran? Any recent plan changes for this account in March? @mike_billing can you take a look?
emily_cs: Invoice JSON attached to the support ticket (ticket #SUP-12487). Dashboard query: standard /billing/overview aggregation for March. They say dashboard shows tokens + embeddings + credits already applied.
metering-bot: invoice-service: generated invoice INV-2026-03-31-54321 for account 54321 at 2026-03-31T23:58:12Z (total $12,345.67)
raj_support: OK. Quick triage — two common causes: late ingested usage after invoice generation OR proration/plan-change edge-case. Mike, any plan migrations for acct 54321 in March?
mike_billing: acct 54321 had a plan upgrade from "pro" -> "pro_plus" on 2026-03-29T14:03:05Z (user-initiated via billing UI). There was a proration applied per our policy. I don't see an explicit credit after 3/31 but will double-check ledger.
raj_support: I'm going to recompute raw usage aggregation from events table ignoring proration to compare. Run this to get raw token sums:

```
SELECT usage_type, SUM(tokens) AS tokens_sum
FROM `prod_metering.events`
WHERE account_id = 54321
  AND event_time >= '2026-03-01'
  AND event_time < '2026-04-01'
GROUP BY usage_type;
```

raj_support: Preliminary run shows tokens=25,412, embeddings=1,240.
emily_cs: Dashboard shows tokens billed: 24,980 and embeddings: 1,240. So tokens delta ~432 tokens -> monetary delta ≈ $358.27 (matches invoice vs dashboard gap roughly).
mike_billing: That 432 extra tokens smells like double-counting during the plan change window. We had one known bug where the plan mapping table returned both old_plan_id and new_plan_id for an event exactly at the boundary when plan_effective_ts was inclusive on both sides.
oliver_oncall: I pulled the metering ingestion logs around 2026-03-29T14:00-14:10. Saw a consumer restart and a replay of a micro-batch. Sample logs:

```
2026-03-29T14:03:06Z metering-consumer INFO processed batch id=cb7a9 reqs=1200 dedup_key=NULL
2026-03-29T14:03:07Z metering-consumer WARN consumer-restart detected, replaying batch cb7a9
2026-03-29T14:03:08Z metering-consumer INFO processed batch id=cb7a9 reqs=1200 dedup_key=present
```

oliver_oncall: The consumer typically attaches request_id for dedupe; looks like a short window where dedupe key was missing for ~1200 events. Not all of those belong to Acme but a subset did, likely causing ~432 tokens to be counted twice.
mike_billing: That maps with the plan-change bug too — if the same event was processed twice and the plan mapping logic treated one as part of "pro" and the other as "pro_plus" due to boundary confusion, we'd see double billing.
sophie_finance: If that's the case, we need to issue an adjustment credit on the invoice for the duplicated charge. Can someone recompute the exact token overlap and dollar amount? I can prepare a credit memo once we have the figure.
raj_support: I'll run a dedupe-aware aggregation to quantify duplicates by request_id. Query:

```
WITH dedup AS (
  SELECT request_id, usage_type, SUM(tokens) as tokens
  FROM `prod_metering.events`
  WHERE account_id=54321
    AND event_time >= '2026-03-29T13:55:00'
    AND event_time < '2026-03-29T14:10:00'
  GROUP BY request_id, usage_type
)
SELECT SUM(tokens) as tokens_total, COUNT(*) as distinct_requests
FROM dedup
WHERE request_id IS NOT NULL;
```

raj_support: Result: tokens_total = 1,820; distinct_requests = 420. Cross-checking against non-dedup run gives tokens_total_raw = 2,252 -> delta = 432 tokens.
mike_billing: Great — matches the discrepancy. Dollar value = 432 tokens * token_rate($0.83/100 tokens) = ~$3.58? Wait that's off. Our token pricing is per 1,000 tokens; check plan-specific rate. Using acct 54321 effective rate $0.83 per 1k tokens -> 432 * 0.00083 = $0.35856. Hmm invoice gap is $358.27 not $0.36. Looks like tokens here are weighted by model type and context windows. Need to map tokens->dollar per event.
raj_support: Right — some events were long-context and billed at different per-token multipliers. I'll join to raw_event_metadata to calculate billed_amount:

```
SELECT SUM(billed_amount) as billed_total_dup
FROM (
  SELECT request_id, SUM(billed_amount) as billed_amount
  FROM `prod_metering.events`
  WHERE account_id=54321
    AND event_time >= '2026-03-29T13:55:00'
    AND event_time < '2026-03-29T14:10:00'
  GROUP BY request_id
) WHERE request_id IN (
  SELECT request_id FROM `prod_metering.events`
  GROUP BY request_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
);
```

raj_support: That returns billed_total_dup = $358.27
sophie_finance: Perfect. That's the number. We should issue a credit for $358.27 on INV-2026-03-31-54321 and patch the invoice notes to explain root cause: transient ingestion replay + dedupe key missing + plan boundary mapping. I'll draft the memo.
mike_billing: I'll open a PR to make plan_effective_ts semantics exclusive on the previous plan (end is exclusive) and add additional integration tests for consumer restarts so dedupe_key is always populated. Also adding a short-term mitigation: re-run a backfill to drop duplicates before future invoice generation windows.
oliver_oncall: I've scheduled a backfill job to run tonight that will create a correction record set for affected accounts. I'll also add an alert when the dedupe_key null rate > 0.1% per minute.
emily_cs: I'll reply to the customer with an ETA: we will post a credit of $358.27 to your account and update the invoice notes. Apologize for the disruption — we'll share a short postmortem once fixes are in.
sophie_finance: Action items: Mike -> code fix + tests (P0), Oliver -> backfill + alert (P0), Raj -> produce final duplicate list and credit amount confirmation (P1), Sophie -> create credit memo and apply (P1). Emily -> customer comms.
emily_cs: Thanks team. I'll update the ticket and ping once the credit is issued. :thumbsup:
